spans.text: Haiti’s gang‑driven massacre in Kenscoff keeps escalation risk elevated but its forward momentum is constrained by limited gang capacity and UN investigations.

**Mass casualties and large‑scale kidnapping:** On 23 August, gangs killed at least 47 people, injured 22 and abducted more than 50 in Kenscoff, a fact reported by the United Nations and echoed across multiple outlets (AP 3 September 2026 [3]; Tribune 2026‑09‑01 [7]; African News 2026‑08‑31 [9]; African News 2026‑08‑31 [10]).

**Continued hostage‑taking of foreign nationals:** Two South Korean workers kidnapped on 31 July were released in mid‑August, underscoring the gangs’ capacity to target nationals (Yonhap 2 September 2026 [5]).

**Limited gang capacity and external scrutiny:** Witnesses noted reconnaissance drones before the attack, yet UN officials report that only eight armored vehicles were present, highlighting a shortfall in protective assets (Tribune 2026‑09‑01 [7]). Ongoing UN investigations and international attention act as a brake on further escalation.
